plans.note: Section 15 is captioned as a one-way limitation of Garman's liability; check cap amount, mutuality and whether IP indemnity (sec-13), confidentiality (sec-14) and wilful misconduct are carved out.
Section 13 is the vendor IP indemnity; confirm defence/settlement control, procedure and that it is not capped or gutted by sec-15, and check for any reciprocal indemnity imposed on Sparkling.
No non-compete heading; if any restraint on Sparkling's business or sourcing of competing software exists it would sit in the use restrictions (sec-3) or general matters (sec-20).
Nothing signals exclusivity; scan the licence grant, use restrictions and maintenance/fees provisions for sole-source or 'all requirements' language.
MFN would most likely appear in the fees or maintenance pricing terms; only flag if it obliges Sparkling to extend best terms to Garman.
Section 19 is squarely on point; test duration, whether it binds Sparkling (likely mutual), scope of covered employees and any general-advertising/unsolicited-response carve-out.
Section 17 governs term and termination; also review the rejection option (sec-7/sec-8) and maintenance cancellation rights, and confirm no penalty on our exit and no vendor walk-away mid-term.
Look for maintenance auto-renewal and notice window in sec-10/sec-17 and any renewal price uplift in the fees section (sec-11).
Governing law, venue and any arbitration clause will sit in general matters (sec-20), spanning pages 10-11; confirm the jurisdiction is on the accepted list and disputes go to courts.
Assignment is typically in sec-20; also check the licence grant (sec-2) for transfer restrictions and sec-17 for any termination right triggered by our change of control.

Confirm Garman retains only its own software IP and that Sparkling's data, configurations and any custom modifications/deliverables (see sec-4 conversion work and sec-16 escrow) are not assigned to Garman.
Section 2 is the grant; test coverage of affiliates, authorized locations (see sec-6) and outsourced contractors, plus whether the licence is perpetual/irrevocable rather than revocable at will.
Any licence-verification audit right would attach to the use restrictions (sec-3) or general matters; if present, check notice, frequency, business-hours limits and who bears cost.
Watch for late-payment interest, early-termination charges or stipulated damages payable by Sparkling in the fees and termination sections; credits running to us are acceptable.
Section 12 covers specifications and warranty; check warranty duration from acceptance (sec-6), the remedy offered, and interaction with maintenance (sec-10) and the rejection option (sec-7).
No insurance heading; Garman personnel will be on site for installation and training (sec-4, sec-5, sec-9), so if nothing appears in general matters this is a gap to raise.
Check the fees schedule and maintenance terms for minimum licence counts, committed maintenance years or take-or-pay volumes binding Sparkling.

Post-termination effects and survival sit in sec-17/sec-18; source code escrow (sec-16) is partial continuity only — confirm return of Sparkling data and migration assistance, otherwise treat as missing.
